gen-dafont-visitor-gf-inter-tight: Visitor pulls every stroke like solder through a nozzle. Inter Tight underneath is a sans with short ascenders barely poking above its lowercase, so paragraphs settle into a tidy, tightly packed texture.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-karla: Karla is a stocky, approachable sans-serif whose middle band runs so tall the lines look sturdy. Karla stays low-key while Visitor keeps a tube-like thickness through every bend and does the showing off.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-khula: Visitor hangs rope-like stems up top while the text below reads modern, with a tall squat midsection. Khula keeps its curves open, so paragraphs move along smoothly without snagging.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-krub: Nostalgic and digital up top, Visitor draws no pinched joints or flared ends. Krub brings pen-lifted curves and a pronounced x-height, a contemporary sans-serif that stays out of the way.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-kufam: Visitor pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle, leaving the e gaping. Kufam, a sans-serif with generously open curves, handles the steady text while Visitor grabs the attention.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-lexend: Lexend offers outsized lowercase with open jaws on every curve, a friendly sans-serif. Lexend keeps its thickness put around curves, a quiet foil for Visitor and its pulled-solder strokes.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-lexend-deca: Clean and approachable, Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line. Beneath the nostalgic, digital Visitor headings, its big lowercase and short-stopping terminals let paragraphs roll along without any fuss.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-liter: Liter reads modern and businesslike, its strokes uniform and its lowercase carrying great vertical presence. And Visitor earns its keep big and short, where its gaping e can show off.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-mada: Approachable and modern, the text here has a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close. Mada lets Visitor stay the star, its line steady and pressure-free, while the body does the quiet work.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-martel-sans: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor draws every glyph in a single-width stroke. Martel Sans, with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line, lets paragraphs unspool without friction.
